question.text: A person of mass 50 kg stands on a platform of mass 25 kg. Holding one end of a rope that runs through a set of frictionless pulleys attached to the platform and to a fixed support, he pulls the rope. With what pulling force must he pull for the platform to rise at a constant speed?
conditions: platform moves upward at a steady, constant speed
person stands on the platform while pulling the rope

figure.description: Three pulleys are used. Two pulleys, ceiling pulley 1 (left) and ceiling pulley 2 (right), are fixed to an overhead support. A third pulley, the platform pulley, is fixed to the platform on a short post at its left edge, at a height below the two ceiling pulleys. One end of the rope is tied off at the overhead support next to ceiling pulley 1. From that fixed end the rope runs straight down and passes under the platform pulley, goes back up and over ceiling pulley 1, runs across and over ceiling pulley 2, and then comes straight down to the person's hand; the person stands on the platform and pulls this final end.

solution.approach: Trace the rope through the pulleys to count how many rope segments pull upward on the person-and-platform system, then balance that total pull against the total weight.

steps.text: Follow the rope: it is tied to the fixed ceiling support, runs down to the pulley mounted on the platform, wraps under it, runs back up to a ceiling pulley, across to a second ceiling pulley, and down to the person's hand.
steps.equation: one continuous rope, tension T throughout, since the pulleys are frictionless

steps.text: Two of the rope segments pull straight up on the pulley fixed to the platform, and the segment coming down to the person's hand pulls straight up on the person. All three segments carry the same tension T.
steps.equation: total upward pull on the person-and-platform system = T + T + T = 3T

steps.text: The platform moves up at a steady rate, so the system is in equilibrium: the total upward pull equals the total weight of the person and platform.

common_mistakes.text: Counting only the two rope segments on the platform's own pulley and missing the segment pulling up on the person's hand gives 2T = 750 N, so T = 375 N.
